title: Clue(do): Third Best Board Game Ever
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the board game Clue (Cluedo). They cover its invention by Anthony E. Pratt and Elda Pratt during World War II, the early Murder prototype, the Waddington's and Parker Brothers publishing deals, Pratt's modest royalties and obscure death, and the game's popularity. They explain the classic rules (suspects, weapons, rooms, suggestions and disproving), deduction and note-taking strategy, and an AI and Duke University algorithm for the game. They go over international name variations, the many editions and updates, spin-offs, and the 1985 movie Clue with its three alternate endings and cast. The episode ends with a listener correction about Michiko Kakutani's gender.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck welcome listeners, joke about Clue characters, and Chuck mentions bidding on a 1972 edition of Clue.

segments.title: Clue cover photo spoof
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1972 Clue box cover photo and a Medium spoof article about its photo shoot that they could not verify.

segments.title: Anthony Pratt's early life and murder parlor game
segments.summary: Clue's origin begins with Anthony E. Pratt, a Birmingham-born piano player who played a game called murder as a teen and later performed at hotel murder mystery nights. During World War II blackouts, he and his wife Elda developed the game.

segments.title: Early Clue prototype and Waddington's deal
segments.summary: The original game was called Murder and had ten characters, nine weapons, including an Irish shillelagh. The Pratts met with Waddington's through friend Jeffrey Bull, who sold the game to them. A patent came in 1947 and production began around 1949. The name Cluedo came from Latin 'ludo' meaning 'I play'.

segments.title: Parker Brothers and house inspirations
segments.summary: Parker Brothers renamed the game Clue in the US. Differences between UK and US versions are noted, such as Reverend Green. The UK and US houses supposedly inspired by Tudor Close in Sussex and George Parker's New Hampshire estate.

segments.title: Pratt's royalties and obscure death
segments.summary: Pratt sold overseas rights in 1953 for five thousand pounds, and his royalty checks stopped around 1965. He died in 1994. Waddington's did not know he had died, and they searched for him for a sales celebration press release. His gravestone is described.

segments.title: Clue popularity and ranking
segments.summary: Clue is described as one of the most popular board games, ranked among the top five, and Josh calls it the third most popular game. They mention an upcoming Scrabble episode idea.

segments.title: Transition and personal board game memories
segments.summary: The hosts share personal memories of playing board games and discuss a game of Clue at home with Emily.

segments.title: How to play Clue: setup and suggestions
segments.summary: Players choose one of six suspects and the game uses six weapons and nine rooms. Three hidden cards identify the murderer, weapon, and room. Players move, enter a room, and make suggestions that players to their left must disprove by showing one matching card.

segments.title: Accusations and staying in after elimination
segments.summary: A player can make an accusation at any time, and if correct they win. Eliminated players still enjoy watching the game. The hosts compare this to Twitch-style game watching.

segments.title: Clue strategy and note-taking
segments.summary: The hosts discuss strategies drawn from online forums: using suggestions to eliminate cards, varying suggestions to avoid tipping off opponents, and noting which cards each player has shown.

segments.title: Deduction, AI, and Duke University algorithm
segments.summary: Clue is described as a logic problem. Dutch computer scientist Hans van den Herik formalized it for AI, and Duke University developed an algorithm to solve it, with possible applications to robotic mine sweeping.

segments.title: Sponsor-free transition to international names
segments.summary: Transition from strategy into international variations of the game.

segments.title: International character names
segments.summary: Names differ across countries, including Doctor Black in the UK, Reverend Green, and Baroness von Blau in Brazil. Josh comments on the Madame Curry name in Norway and Switzerland.

segments.title: Clue editions and updates
segments.summary: Discussion of material changes over time, updated character backstories, the 2008 Discover the Secrets edition, and the 2023 update that restored classic names and characters.

segments.title: Clue spin-offs and licensed versions
segments.summary: Licensed versions include an Alfred Hitchcock Clue and Scooby-Doo and Golden Girls versions. Hasbro owns the IP, and there is a UK game show, a book series, a VCR game, and an animated series planned.

segments.title: Clue 1985 movie
segments.summary: The 1985 film Clue, co-written and directed by Jonathan Lynn, is discussed, including its three alternate endings and the cast, including Tim Curry, Madeline Kahn, Christopher Lloyd, and Martin Mull.

segments.title: Listener correction on Michiko Kakutani
segments.summary: A listener writes to correct an earlier episode, noting that the literary critic Michiko Kakutani is a woman, and the hosts acknowledge the mistake.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners, invite corrections by email, and give closing credits.
